item.title: Re: Mothers Know Best
item.content:encoded:
(disclaimer: it is not lost on me that this is a sensitive topic. As a trans individual myself, it is my intention to play on the horror of a transphobic mother/daughter relationship, and not to merely act out conversion therapy.)

I'm glad you're aware of the risks involved in tackling this kind of subject matter. LGBT-trauma-as-horror can be done successfully, but it's a real tightrope.

Overall I think the concept has strong potential for great horror and impactful storytelling, though I recommend against using all three case studies. By trying to squeeze every possible angle out of your concept, you run the risk of causing each segment's impact to be diluted from the overstuffing of the article as a whole. The first case you described definitely sounds like the strongest of the bunch. Focus on telling that story well and doing it justice and you'll have a winner. The second case could maybe be included briefly to act as a foil to the first case, but I wouldn't say it's strictly necessary.

Greenlight granted.

item.title: Re: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone
item.content:encoded:
Have been summoned by PM, so here I come. Pighead In, here's a short review of your draft.

So, this is pretty good when it comes to the writing, but I have two issues with it. The first, the main one, is the fact that for me, the end is really abrupt. The entire thing is pretty short and when I came to the end of the interview, I was like "That's all?". I felt like there were more things that you could tell, about why SCP XXX-1 wants to find love, about the feelings of isolation it could have (and who were really briefly touched upon on the very last sentence).

And the second thing is that at this moment, for me, this draft is "Mermaid, but SCP". Like, I feel like I just see a mermaid who is adapted into an SCP. And not that I'm against mythological creatures being turned into SCPs, the history of the site had proved that it could work really efficiently. But with the really short draft, that creates a situation when it's not really interesting to see this, it's like "So, here's this mythological creature and its abilities and nothing else".

What I can suggest to you is to dig deeper into how the mermaids live as a society, what are their collective purpose in life and what is the backstory of SCP-XXXX-1, what are the events who led it to wanting a mate, a person to love, what led it to wanting not just having intercourse, but having a person for spending the rest of its life with. With that, you have the potential to tell a pretty good story about how isolation and being tired of just doing what you have to do can led you to wanting something new in life and experiencing, for the first time, human feelings.

So, think about all that, for the rest, your writing has potential. It's all for me, Pighead Out.

item.title: Re: Love at Long Last
item.content:encoded:
This isn't my original story: I received the idea from this youtube video…

There's a fine line between inspiration and plagiarism—all writers get inspiration from other stories and there's nothing truly original under the sun, but the new piece has to set itself apart from the source it's drawing from. Whether or not it succeeds at that is usually very subjective.

I watched the video. It's a very good story. My concern is that you run the risk of hewing too closely to the original writing while still changing enough plot elements to take the impact out of. Dear Nia works so well not because of the global stakes with the destruction of Soren's Earth, but the emotional conflict that arises from two opposing points of view. In my opinion, that feels much more emotionally complex (and therefore more resonant) than the basic "Desire > Recklessness > Regret" arc you've outlined above.

The ending sounds pretty flat, what with one character vanishing with no explanation and the other one ending up in Foundation custody to act as an exposition machine. Consider what other outcomes may arise for them. I like the idea of an RMK-Class Scenario getting thrown into the mix; to me that's the most intriguing part of your idea and potentially its greatest strength, so I recommend you focus on developing that aspect of the plot and its ramifications on both the world and its characters.

item.title: Roland The Headless Thompson Gunner
item.content:encoded:
The idea of a vengeance-driven headless specter has been around for a long time, although one mister horseman is by far the most well-known. I like the idea of a (relatively) modern take, and Warren Zevon came through to give me a good starting point, as the song already contains the basics for a good story. Plus, it's a good match for my signature mix of weirdness and character-driven stories.

https://youtu.be/wRWCK9zGynA

I'm hoping to tell the initial history of the anomaly and its assumed source in the description and logs, and how it hunted down its targets in conprocs and logs. For instance, detailing the response to a manifestation and how to not get shot by it, and which specific types of areas are most likely to have the thing appear.

As for the rest of the story, after it gets revenge I think it would be neat if the headless gunner shut down for a while. Formerly a mercenary, then driven to seek out revenge for itself, without any sort of personal gain it would just… stop. Until something awakens it again, and the eternal Thompson gunner learns to fight for other's sake. This I would probably explore through addenda and in-universe page revisions.

Thoughts? Anything I can explain further? Any response is appreciated greatly.

item.title: SCP Idea - Algernon-13
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi, Light horror

Elevator Pitch: A dim, distant star is discovered by a group of astronomers who discover that, when extensively gazed upon, said star can temporarily impart seemingly supernatural enhancements to the viewer. Said enhancements come at a price, however.

Central Narrative: A small research team in Argentina discovers a hitherto unknown star. The initial astronomer who extensively gazes at the star notes a small mote of light in the corner of his eye, though the light dissipates after several hours, since he chooses to ignore it. His partner, however, continues to be bothered by the light in the corner of her eye and keeps staring at it. Once she stares at it for an arbitrary amount of time, she suddenly seizes a marker and begins scribbling strange symbols on a whiteboard. This fit lasts for approximately thirteen hours before she collapses from exhaustion. When she reawakens, she realizes that her knowledge of mathematics and science has been dramatically reduced to roughly that of a first-grade level.

SCP is made aware of this development and has its own team investigate the star, which has been designated Algernon-13 (after the novel "Flowers for Algernon"). Numerous personnel undergo tests, including a former soldier (who experiences increased aggression and muscle growth), a linguist (who briefly becomes an onmiglot), and an artist (who paints gorgeous pictures unlike any she'd ever made before, and which offers some insight into the nature of the star), all of whom suffer severe degradation after thirteen hours have passed. It also becomes apparent that the star is attempting to communicate in some way, and the SCP would detail their efforts to figure out what the star wants.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook involves the mystery behind why the star induces "attribute enhancements" on its viewers. The mystery reaches its zenith with the pictures painted by the artist, as they give a nebulous picture of what's going on around the star, leaving one with as many new questions as answers.

Additional Notes: Not sure what to rate this anomaly - Euclid or Keter class. Suggestions would be helpful.

item.title: Re: The 7th Panzer Divison
item.content:encoded:
A slight revision I made as a further development of this idea. I took out the part of the Obskuracorps but not sure if it would have been better to try and fit it in some how.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): History, Ghost

Elevator Pitch: A group of ex-nazis with a Panzer III are given the ability to spawn an entire division of ghost tanks after being recovered by SCP agents during a mission.

**Central Narrative:**
**Central Narrative:**

In 1944, a group of german tank crew abandon the nazi cause and fled into the wilderness with a Panzer III. They survive by scavenging for food and going on raids against villages for supplies, unaware that the war is over and unsure of what is to become of them if they surrender, the tank crew refuse to return to the post-wwii Europe.

As time goes on, dissidence begins to grow in each of them against the former regime they served, throwing away their black and red armband, scratching off symbols of the old regime and discard anything else that has little functional purpose such as decorations, uniform insignia, etc keeping only the necessary items needed for survival.

During a containment breach at a nearby facility, a massive, bottomless sinkhole is formed taking the tank along with her crew with it to the bottom. Surprisingly, they survive the fall but find themselves in a world similar to our own, a damp, dark, cold world lacking any source of light. The hole they arrived from now appears as a tiny white dot surrounded by a sky of total darkness. As the group ventures throughout this “underworld,” they discover that it’s populated entirely by dark, shadowy beings that bear a disfigured, grainy, slender silhouette of a human. Worst yet is that they seem to be on the hunt for the tank crew.

Looking for a way out and forced to survive in this new world against these creatures, the tank crew utilize what limited ammunition and supply they have left on them to ensure the safety of their survival. Eventually, the tank that they utilized began to slowly change, with deep scratch marks being discovered both inside and outside the tank. The tank crew were ready to abandon the tank thinking that it was beginning to wear down until the radio man discovered that using the radio at a certain frequency would spawn a massive tank army consisting of only the limited WWII German tanks built during that era, with mighty caliber guns capable of toppling the deadliest war machines ever built and armour that could withstand the might of Zeus.

Decades later, an investigation into the sinkhole would commence by SCP agents. After multiple explorations, the panzer crew would be discovered and brought back to the surface, hands in the air appearing as though they haven’t aged a day since 1944. After reappearing from the underworld, the tank crew would utilize their tank army as a show of defiance against their new captors, only to realize that the former tank army that was made of the toughest armour had become a hazey, transparent division. Objects would come and go through the ghost's armour as tank shells would come roaring, crashing into the ground leaving no bodies to be found and only a crater in it’s spot. The screams of horrors by soldiers being gunned down and mutilated would play as they rolled past, deafening the hollowing engines of the tanks.

The tank crew would eventually be captured by MTF-Mu-13 and held in captivity by SCP researchers putting an end to their escape. Days later, multiple reports of “ghost tanks” would appear throughout Europe and North Africa, firing upon civilian homes, shopping centers, gas stations and random buildings leaving destruction and tens to hundreds of casualties with zero traces of the ghosts left. An interview conducted on the tank crew would show similarities in both their journey in the underworld and the aforementioned incidents in terms of behaviour, actions and locations.

item.title: Mildly Reluctant -1
item.content:encoded:
Maybe I'd view this differently if I'd read the original article first, but this doesn't do anything for me. Sorry.

+ Some critique
- Close

So there's a cat that turns living things to stone, as well as anything they're touching out to a meter. Fortunately this only affects living things, so the cat can still eat… except bacteria are living things, so presumably the cat has no microbiota and should not be able to digest. Maybe I'm overthinking it, but that's how I do.

Aside from that, when Boyd turned to stone, he fell up. No reason why, it's thus far unrepeatable, and there's that problem with the maths not adding up to his distance. It just seems like a second anomaly that got tagged on without a proper connection. It also seems like a wasted opportunity, since a cat that consistently turns living things into flying statues (or cut out the stone bit and it just makes things fly away) is more interesting to me. I like the idea of a cute little kitten that goes around rubbing on people's legs for attention, but if someone actually stops to pet it, or happens to be wearing shorts, they go orbital.

Lastly, I didn't enjoy the interview log. Just not my kind of cheese, I guess.

This did inspire a little headcanon for me though, where the same person/group is responsible for all ageless anomalous animals (3828 is the only other one I can think of offhand, but there's gotta be more).

item.title: The Lightswitch
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror (?)

Page Layout (Optional): Brief SCP article with most content being in Addendum

Elevator Pitch: A lightswitch that, when flicked on, gives the user life and, when flicked off, takes the user’s life. Things get more interesting when living creatures turn it on and dead creatures turn it off.

Central Narrative: The SCP is simple enough; if you flick it off, it takes your consciousness, rendering you essentially dead/vegative. If someone forces your corpse/vegative body to flick it on again, you gain your consciousness back.

The Foundation recovers the SCP from a GOI (likely MC&D) after someone in the GOI unwittingly flicked it on while alive, causing the user to take the previous user’s consciousness and turn into a human with two minds, with two separate consciousnesses and all of it’s memories and skills. The GOI then used this to its own advantage, killing targets and employees with high levels of skill/competence/important memories and then adding them to some central source (becoming a sort of librarian/bookkeeper of minds). The bookkeeper is then interviewed by the Foundation, and is very resilient to giving up any information related to the GOI. Forcing a corpse to switch it off creates a “black hole” of consciousness, as the lightswitch attempts to drain the corpse of consciousness but finds nothing. The corpse then becomes SCP-XXXX-2, which constantly emits an aura of consciousness drain around it, slowly draining those within range of intelligence, reaction speed, emotional response and memories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Keeping it short and simple, with an addendum explaining the GOI’s usage and recovery notes.

Additional Notes: I imagine the article itself will be brief (here is a lightswitch, it turns people on and off, no testing allowed, etc) with an addendum that holds the real meat of the SCP (recovery, interview).

In the interview, the Bookkeeper explains that he is the third iteration of them, and continuously absorbs the previous one before him. He mentions that plans were in place to try and create a sort of “generational immortality”, although they didn’t get very far.

The Foundation seriously considers having the captured Bookkeeper forcibly switching it off, then having one of their own agents/D-Class flick it on to take all the previous memories, however they get denied out of the fear that the new personalities may be overwhelming/resistant, and they would just end up back where they started, with another Bookkeeper that refuses to cooperate.

item.title: Just The Two Of Us
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Bits of Horror and Action.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is that a large humanoid creature is found accompanied with a feline in which they seemed to hold a link where the former guards the latter in an overprotective style.
This meaning that anything that draws close to the cat would be considered a potential threat if it was the first time encountering one another and multiple, timed sessions would need to be implemented before the human comes off its high guard.
Before containment this would be how the specimens got their food as the harmless looking cat would lure in people who stumbled into secluded areas only to be snatched up by the humanoid creature for a quick kill and feast during the early hours.
However both appear to harness a certain weakness to nature so wood, fruit or vegetables would render them either weakened or agitated depending on the dosage provided at that time making it a good counter measure during a containment breach if used properly.
The level of understanding held by both specimens could be exploited by persuading them into helping the facility when keeping other SCPs secured or when cross testing to give varying results due to how differently the two may react in different situations. The human helping to dispatch or beat back threats whilst the cat can provide comfort to those panicking as long as the two are kept relatively close to one another. It would require training and bargaining, though.

Central Narrative: The two would originally be found within a town after multiple disappearance are reported only for a task force to discover the hideout of the anomalies until they come to a conclusion that suits the both of them. After being well contained in their new home they seem relatively fine with their living arrangements but soon begin asking for more things in exchange for doing tasks or participating in cross testing procedures when being asked about it. This would lead to contained cross testing between different SCPs of the human's capabilities once in an enraged form after the cat is removed from the select distance previously set up with cross testing the cat with safe class human SCPs to see if progress can be made with them in any way. Conversation would spark up about how the humanoid's strength seemed to be enough to counter even keter class SCPs and potential to manipulate it into helping out task forces could be considered in upcoming missions.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bond between the two being demonstrated only to be used by the foundation to create a weapon out of the humanoid creating a blackmail scenario where it tries to be with its cat once again whilst remaining within the rules it agreed to. Not to mention, the diverse between understanding and blind rage it has to swap constantly between if it doesn't want to risk being terminated by either the SCPs or the scientists that have it under lock and key. Meanwhile the cat sits inside the once lively containment cell awaiting its other half's return or plotting an escape by clawing into the wooden walls and being forced to further develop its anomalous abilities such as the bell being shaken more to amplify the effects it currently has. All the while it isn't considered what might happen if one were to perish considering how close they both are even though they both subtly drop hints of great evil erupting from within the other if it were to happen.

item.title: Accessible Issue
item.content:encoded:
Hello,

So the SCP Foundation is an incredible premise that can create some unique stories based on it’s premise alone. That being said, as someone who has now made multiple attempts at SCP’s I’d like to talk about some issues I see in the sight as an outsider.

+ Greenlight Troubles
- Greenlight Troubles

The site’s process for creating new SCPs, especially for new creators, is close focused at best. The fictional Foundation is supposed to be a clinical world facing fantastical elements, but as someone coming in, the similarities to the real site are a bit unnerving. To say nothing of the users, from personal experience they are fine, and sometimes friendly, this is purely about how a brand new author. To give credit, yes an author can develop ideas outside the site plenty, but that doesn't change they then have to convince at least two reviewers in a small paragraph there idea is worth it. Not impossible, obviously, but a little convoluted. I think the ability for more freedom in trying to convey what makes an idea worth it could benefit this site greatly. Once again: this spot isn’t impossible, but cam present real problems to someone in trying to cram an idea into a small format.

+ Aaaand its gone
- Aaaand its gone

The rating system means with -10 likes, a page meets the criteria for deletion. Now again, I can appreciate the benefits of running a strict site, but something about this seems a little cruel. For a site requiring hard work from new creators, all it takes is ten people deciding to press a button saying they didn’t like it, and that says to the author this page is worthy of deletion. It could be absolutely certain that if every site had a shallow enough criteria, many beloved posts would be gone before they blew up. Im not saying enough downvotes isn’t indicative of a post possibly needing deletion, but maybe that particular field needs to be stretched, and authors in general given a chance. After all theres no way to actually know if the majority of site users dislike an SCP, the votes are only indicative of the people who found that page.

+ Slightly Personal
- slightly personal

Once again, I’m sure to some this seems like the ravings of a writer who was a little hurt, and in some part I give credit that it does come from that. More so though, I’d argue that this is also the perspective of someone who has worked hard to try and join really creative people, and been turned away not necessarily by them, but by a system coming across as super insular. It occurs to me maybe I’m also ridiculous for trying to join a catalogue cresting the 6000’s, but under the impression that this universe could be even more I did wanna try. Definitely some fault is mine in writing, lets not pretend any old SCP’s I made would be the next 096, but my point lies in that: in trying to add to something I’ve seen as fun and a little silly, I’ve been met with an incredibly high wall, in some ways earned by the site, but in many ways just as ridiculous.

In closing: the site’s a little too insular. This doesn’t necessarily warrant a whole overhaul, but maybe a reflective look at how some things should be run. I suppose if you want to write this off as a newbee venting, thats fine, but I think it would great benefit the Foundation to genuinely look at how it handles new ideas, and what kind of criteria it has, and whether or not its always fair.

item.title: Re: Hikikomori
item.content:encoded:
The original idea was simple, but then I need some mechanics to make it happen. The "transport to another reality" bit was inspired by these two images:

https://i.ytimg.com/vi/LdCWEWzcedw/hqdefault.jpg
https://i.imgur.com/FG7oz2s.jpg

The sci-fi begins with the question: what if this actually worked? Or better, it seemed to work initially, but was reversed?

Suicide because I need some way to express that utter desperation that a hikikomori might feel, and also to set the tone. However, I don't want to use these specific pictures because of copyright reasons, and I have no need to involve any specific outside lore.

The similarity to Freddy Krueger or any other pop culture is coincidental. Freddy Krueger is a villain, the protagonist here is a essentially a victim, or thrown about by events like the protagonist in the film "12 Monkeys". I realized I might have to edit the draft to underline this point.

The anomaly is exhibited with self-imposed isolation because it needs an altered state of mind not available otherwise.

Hey, it's me, WizzBlizz, here to give you some crit!

Line By Line
Line By Line

I'll be doing line-by-line suggestions as I read through the article, so also consider this to be first impressions.

and converted to Site-090

Why not just Site-90? Seems like a weird name.

No personnel are allowed to enter SCP-4085 without authorization from the Director of Site-090.

Maybe specify the Site Director's name?

attempting to exit with items from SCP-4085 without purchasing,

Awkward wording. Just say 'stealing'.

a standard size grocery store

grocery stores come in many shapes and sizes, so I'm not sure what "standard" means here.

observed to have standard grocery store stock,

Again, different grocery stores have different items. Especially if you go to a different region or country.

The packaging of products such as chips or cookies appears normal, but when opened it can be observed that the contents are in the shape of human extremities such as fingers, noses, and tongues.

This is too many words to just say there are cookies in the shapes of fingers and tongues.

Analysis of the meat products found in SCP-4085 shows that they are genetically identical to human.

Just say the meat products are genetically identical to humans.

Analysis of packaged food products and produce inside SCP-4085 are normal,

normal how so? Haven't we established already that everything is shaped like humans? what food products are we actually talking about here? Does this include the meat products?

SCP-4085-A is the designation for the entities that exist inside SCP-4085

Again, you can simplify this like:

SCP-4085-A are [description of anomaly] that exist within SCP-4085

When observed from inside SCP-4085, they are humanoid in shape, but are 3 meters in height, have orange-tinted skin,

What does "humanoid in shape" mean? humanoid is a shape. Also, scrap the "but". Not sure why that is there.

If a subject causes a Σ-Window Shopper event

How do you cause one?

This will continue until the subject(s), who have not met the criteria, have been subdued.

What "criteria" are we talking about?

[See Investigation Log]

Just a personal preference, but this would fit better as a footnote.

were given Class B amnestic with false memory implementation.

Awkward phrasing. Try something like:

were administered Class B amnestics, including the construction of new memories.

You know, if you told people what to expect beforehand these expeditions would go a whole lot smoother.

Good point. Why would they not tell them about potentially dangerous anomalies they will be interacting with?

Oh my god… You guys see this right? It has a face. A human face!

They're getting a bit over-excited for a weirdly shaped fruit.

Please approach the entity and attempt to gather information from it.

The dialogue from Dr. Kellogg feels very awkward. When speaking to a D-Class during a mission, they should be clear and concise, rather than overly clinical. In this example, he hasn't even specified how the D-Class is supposed to gather information about it.

We make our fine products by infusing and capturing the finest of lost human souls!

The hook has arrived a bit too late to the party I think.

Well orange man

You can't repeat the same joke twice.

Sick fucking hell!

Very weird phrasing. Not even sure if he's saying something positive or negative.

I don't think these things are trying to help me anymore!

When were they trying to help them? Offering someone products isn't really "helping".

May you please describe what the entities are doing right now?

There is no reason for them to be this polite.

Ow! Fuck! Get off, get off!

This isn't the screaming in pain I would expect to hear from someone getting their leg torn apart.

what was happening to D-1213 could not be determined.

We know, you said it was malfunctioning.

D-rag is a term D-class personnel refer to other new D-class personnel.

This is obvious, no need to tell us.

General Thoughts
General Thoughts

- There are a lot of words you could take out of the description and still have this make just as much sense.
- The article is generally bloated. The Investigations went on for far too long and didn't really tell us anything we didn't already know.
- The dialogue felt very awkward. (I would try saying out loud to see how it feels)
- The idea itself has potential, but the article's bloat means it gets dragged out far too thin.
- I suggest cutting this article down massively and focusing on the core idea.
